intro: Today's updates are headlined by the launch of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and major new partnerships aimed at expanding compute and enterprise capabilities. We also track the latest shifts in productivity tools and the growing infrastructure challenges facing AI energy demands.

must_know.title: GPT-6 Astra: The next generation in intelligence for work
must_know.summary: OpenAI announced GPT-6 Astra, its new business-focused model featuring enhanced reasoning, computer use, and improved judgment.
must_know.why_it_matters: The shift toward models with direct 'computer use' capabilities signals the next major phase of AI-driven enterprise automation.

must_know.title: OpenAI partners with Cerebras
must_know.summary: OpenAI is partnering with Cerebras to secure 750MW of high-speed AI compute power to improve real-time ChatGPT performance.
must_know.why_it_matters: Securing massive, specialized hardware capacity is critical for reducing inference latency in competitive AI markets.

must_know.title: Now everyone can put data to work
must_know.summary: OpenAI introduced a Data agent for ChatGPT Work, allowing users to connect company data and generate interactive dashboards using natural language.
must_know.why_it_matters: This feature lowers the barrier for non-technical users to build tools and extract actionable insights from corporate datasets.

foundation-models.title: Build more natural voice experiences with GPT‑Live‑1 in the API
foundation-models.summary: The GPT-Live-1 model is now available in the OpenAI API, featuring full-duplex voice capabilities, custom voices, and telephony integration.
foundation-models.why_it_matters: This update enables developers to build more natural and responsive voice-based AI applications.

tools.title: Slack can now vibe-code interactive charts and reports inside chats
tools.summary: Slack is introducing 'Slackforce Surfaces,' an AI-powered tool that allows users to generate interactive reports and dashboards via natural language commands.
tools.why_it_matters: The feature demonstrates a shift toward internal 'vibe-coding' to automate data visualization directly within communication platforms.

tools.title: Meta’s Muse AI works and creeps me out
tools.summary: Meta has launched 'Muse,' an AI assistant designed to automate personal productivity tasks like email management, shopping, and travel planning.
tools.why_it_matters: Meta is aggressively moving into the consumer agent space to compete with other integrated productivity AI tools.

hardware.title: Powering AI is an architecture problem
hardware.summary: Infrastructure failures in major data center hubs like Ashburn, Virginia, highlight the increasing fragility of energy grids as AI compute demand rises.
hardware.why_it_matters: Power availability and grid stability are becoming the primary physical constraints on the expansion of large-scale AI clusters.

hardware.title: The iPhone Duo’s hardware doesn’t look special, but its software might be
hardware.summary: The new iPhone Duo enters the foldable market, relying on high-level software polish to differentiate itself from existing Android hardware offerings.
hardware.why_it_matters: Apple's entry into the foldable segment focuses on software-driven UX rather than purely novel hardware specifications.

big-tech.title: Expanding AI access and cyber defense for federal, state, local, and tribal governments
big-tech.summary: OpenAI and the GSA are launching a program to provide governments with $0 license fees, discounted usage, and enhanced cyber defense support.
big-tech.why_it_matters: This subsidization encourages public sector adoption of AI while focusing on security and defense applications.

policy.title: New policy ideas for the Intelligence Age
policy.summary: OpenAI is funding 14 independent projects focused on industrial policy and economic resilience in the era of advanced AI.
policy.why_it_matters: The initiative aims to shape the societal and economic framework of the 'Intelligence Age' through people-first research.

research.title: How AI training scales
research.summary: Researchers have identified gradient noise scale as a metric that predicts the parallelizability of neural network training.
research.why_it_matters: The finding suggests that larger batch sizes can effectively scale training, removing a known bottleneck for future model growth.
